## Natural history notes

A large horse fly characterized by its robust black body, broad dark wings, large eyes, and strong direct flight. In Florida, the Black Horse Fly is found around wetlands, marshes, swamps, ponds, pastures, forest edges, and wooded areas where larvae can develop in moist soil or aquatic-edge habitats. Females take blood meals from mammals and can deliver a painful bite, while males feed on nectar and other sugary resources; the larvae are predatory or scavenging in wet substrates and help link aquatic-edge habitats to the terrestrial food web.
